audit.why: Content 'win' and the full phase sides agree with the packet levelChart at every stage that matters: Jayce owns levels 1-2 before Across the Veil is levelled, Aurora owns 3 through 6, and Jayce reclaims both item stages against her squishy AP frame. No change needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's spike, level-6 and first-item reasons are generic Jayce boilerplate that never names an Aurora ability or a number, and phases[4].why still reads 'six abilities against his four'.
audit.why: Across the Veil is 22/21/20/19/18s and The Weirding is 15/14/13/12/11s — those two timers, not a generic Eclipse line, are what decide when Jayce can step up.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull and the Key Ability Interactions entry; pronoun boilerplate corrected throughout.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Twofold Hunt' is not an Aurora ability — the real Q is Twofold Hex. Worse, the full layer attaches the label '(Blink)' to it and describes it as 'Her escape', which is a different ability entirely: the blink is Across the Veil (W). The name appears 20 times across tldr, winCon, enemyWin, loading, focus.text, four phase reasons, eight breakdown fields, the dos/donts and six report entries.
audit.why: Riot's text: Twofold Hex (Q) is a curse missile with a recast that drags curses back; Across the Veil (W) is the leap that enters the spirit realm. A player told to track 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)' is tracking a fabricated ability and will read the wrong cooldown.
audit.corrected: Every occurrence replaced with Across the Veil (W), which is the ability all the surrounding text actually describes, with its 22s rank-1 cooldown stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions that Across the Veil turns Aurora invisible on landing. It is described only as a blink or dodge.
audit.why: Riot's W text says she enters the spirit realm 'becoming invisible' with bonus move speed. Against Jayce that means she does not merely dodge the orb — she leaves your vision, so the follow-up gate-Q has no target and chasing is a coin flip.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, the Key Ability Interactions entry, dosFull[0] and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: The content 'late' section claims Aurora 'has no sustain'.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration (P) heals her from spirits exorcised by her spells and attacks, and _missing-interactions.json flags this pair for anti-heal. Telling a Jayce player she cannot heal invites him to poke into a bar that refills.
audit.corrected: 'late' rewritten to say the passive trickles health back so poke must be sustained; dontsFull[1].d now names Spirit Abjuration.

audit.whatIsWrong: Aurora is referred to as 'he'/'his' in fifteen full-layer fields, and dosFull[2] / dontsFull[1] carry descriptions copied from unrelated template lines.
audit.why: Wrong pronouns and mismatched title/description pairs read as unmaintained data.
audit.corrected: All pronouns corrected and both descriptions rewritten with real mechanics.

notes: UNVERIFIED, left untouched: the page repeatedly says Aurora ROOTS you — in spikes[1], spikes[2], mid, whys[2], whys[3], whys[5], wants.foe[1] and wants.foe[2]. Riot's text in champ-data/_kits/aurora.json describes no root on any of her five abilities: Q curses, E damages and slows, R shockwaves, slows and creates a slow zone. The kit does carry a hardCC flag on R, but the description mentions only slows, and per the tooltip-parsing caveat I trusted the description. I did NOT rewrite those sentences and I did NOT assert she has no root — the needsResearch block is empty, which means unknown. Someone should confirm what Between Worlds actually applies before this ships, because 'bait the root cooldown' is load-bearing advice on this page. Separately, MC_WR_TABLES.jayce has no aurora row visible in the head of the file while the packet reports 51.74 over 775 games; worth checking the table is complete.
